results.claim: Negative prompts for hands, eyes and bodies are mostly unnecessary from Midjourney v5 and Stable Diffusion XL onward.
Authors report that trained prompt-writing models only bring quality to average and do not beat expert prompt engineering.
For inpainting, prompting only for the erased region works better than prompting for the whole image, in the authors' experience.

limits: No quantitative evaluation: every technique is shown with one or two generated images and the authors' opinion.
Tied to Midjourney v5 / DALL-E / SD of late 2023; features (Zoom Out, Vary Region, /describe, /shorten) are product specific and may have changed.
Unbundling works only for artists famous enough to be described from training data.
Negative prompts are not fully reliable when concepts are strongly correlated.
Legal status of imitating living artists is unsettled; authors advise caution.
practices: Specify the format (stock photo, oil painting, hieroglyph) because it changes style and contents; Format Modifiers.
Format brings its training-data associations (no computers in oil paintings), so combine with other techniques; Format Modifiers.
Name an artist or art movement as a shortcut to a region of latent space; Art Style Modifiers.
Prefer artists who died over a year ago to living artists, and seek legal counsel for commercial use; Art Style Modifiers.
Use /describe to reverse engineer a prompt from an image; Reverse Engineering Prompts.
Append one or two quality boosters (4k, very beautiful, trending on artstation) after the subject, comma separated; Quality Boosters.
Use --no with a comma list to separate intertwined concepts such as oil painting and frame; Negative Prompts.
Put the subject first and use :: weights to mix concepts; Weighted Terms.
Grid search weight combinations at fixed granularity to find the preferred mix; Weighted Terms.
Try stronger negative weights when --no does not remove an unwanted element; Weighted Terms.
Supply a base image link at the start of the prompt (Img2Img) and use a shorter text prompt; Prompting with an Image.
Use inpainting (DALL-E, Vary Region) to change part of an image and prompt only for that part; Inpainting.
Use more than one model, each for what it is best at; Inpainting (Divide Labor).
Use outpainting (Zoom Out, Custom Zoom) to add context or change aspect ratio; Outpainting.
For consistent characters generate two images side by side at 2:1, then inpaint one half per new angle; Consistent Characters.
Rewrite user prompts with another model (e.g. look up the artist's medium, then template {medium} of a {subject} in the style of {artist}); Prompt Rewriting.
Unbundle an artist's style: ask a text model to describe the work without naming the artwork or artist, shorten it, add the subject, then remix components; Meme Unbundling.
Meme mapping: collect prompts from communities (Lexica.art, Discord), and find recurring patterns manually or with NGram analysis or image labelling; Meme Mapping.
Prune prompts with /shorten and token weights, since every added word adds noise; Prompt Analysis.
